title: NASA Has Begun the Countdown to the Launch of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope - Nautilus
gist: NASA has begun the countdown for the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, scheduled to launch August 30 from Kennedy Space Center to detect exoplanets—realizing an idea its namesake first proposed in 1959.

insights.claim: The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is scheduled for liftoff the morning of Sunday, August 30, from Kennedy Space Center in Florida.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Marks the imminent launch of a major new NASA observatory.
insights.locator: scheduled for liftoff the morning of Sunday, August 30th

insights.claim: As early as 1959, Nancy Grace Roman—NASA's first Chief of Astronomy—proposed that space-based telescopes could detect exoplanets by blocking some of the light from stars, the exact approach her namesake telescope is designed to use.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Ties a decades-old scientific proposal directly to the mission's design and objectives.
insights.locator: As early as 1959, Roman proposed that space-based telescopes could be used to detect exoplanets
